description: Every Atera RMM + PSA endpoint, plus a local SQLite mirror that answers fleet-health, SLA, and book-of-business questions no single API call can.

novel_features.name: Dark / stale agents
novel_features.description: Surface agents that have gone quiet — offline or not seen in N days — before the client calls to complain.

novel_features.name: SLA breach-risk ranking
novel_features.description: Rank open tickets by how close they are to breaching first-response or resolution SLA.

novel_features.name: Fleet OS inventory + EOL
novel_features.description: Roll up OS and OS-type counts across the whole estate and flag end-of-life operating systems.

novel_features.name: Book of business
novel_features.description: Per-customer rollup of agent count and contract mix (types + active/inactive) by joining customers, contracts, and agents.

novel_features.name: Technician workload
novel_features.description: Group open tickets and total logged duration by technician to spot who is overloaded.

novel_features.name: Alert triage
novel_features.description: Group open alerts by severity and customer, ranked by age, so the loudest problems surface first.

novel_features.name: Contract coverage gap
novel_features.description: Find under-contracted customers — managed agents with no active recurring or monitoring contract — before the renewal conversation.

novel_features.name: Patch compliance sweep
novel_features.description: Roll up missing-patch counts across the whole estate, ranked by agent and customer, from the per-device patch endpoints.

novel_features.name: What changed since
novel_features.description: Show what was created in a time window — new agents, new tickets, new alerts — across the synced estate.

novel_features.name: Contract expiry calendar
novel_features.description: See which contracts end inside a window, ranked by days-to-expiry and joined to the customer name.

novel_features.name: Estate alert hotspots
novel_features.description: Rank the machines and customers generating the most alerts over a window — the chronic problem devices.
